titleText.es: Y yo podría sustituirte por fotos tuyas antiguas, de cuando parecías feliz.
titleText.en: And I could replace you with older pictures of you, from back when you looked happy.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title text closely translates the official English title text. The raster also localizes the spoken exchange while leaving Photoshop as the established software name.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for us to indulge in; for us to go through (an excessive amount of something)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pegarnos is pegar with nos attached. In pegarse un atracón, it does not mean physically hitting; the whole expression means indulging in or doing far too much of something.

example.es: Decidimos pegarnos un atracón de series.
example.en: We decided to binge on TV series.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: binge; excessive amount done or consumed at once
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Atracón can describe overeating, but it also extends to an excessive burst of another activity. It is masculine: un atracón.

example.es: Se dio un atracón de películas.
example.en: He went on a movie binge.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; introduces the activity or thing involved in a binge
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After atracón, de introduces what was consumed or done excessively. An action can follow in its unchanged dictionary form.

example.es: Nos dimos un atracón de ver películas.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conducir is the unchanged dictionary form. It can name the activity of driving without identifying who performs it.

example.en: I prefer to drive during the day.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cogido is the completed-action form of coger. With haber it forms a completed possibility such as podríamos haber cogido. In much of Latin America coger can sound sexual, but this source uses the ordinary Spain sense “take.”

example.en: We could have taken the train.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With con and a tool, control, or idea, jugar can mean experimenting with it rather than playing a game.

example.es: Voy a jugar con los ajustes de color.
example.en: I am going to play around with the color settings.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: with; introduces what someone experiments with
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In jugar con, con introduces the control, tool, or idea being tried in different ways.
In software or equipment, an ajuste is a setting that changes how something behaves or appears.
Tinte can mean dye or tint. In an image-editing control, it refers to the hue or color cast applied to an image.

example.es: La foto tiene un tinte azul.
example.en: The photo has a blue tint.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Calla tells one friend, relative, or other familiar person to stop talking. It comes from callar.

example.en: Be quiet for a moment, please.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: pegarse un atracón de + cosa o actividad
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you describe indulging in far too much of something at once?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching reflexive form of pegarse, then un atracón de and name the thing or activity.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The person marker changes: me pego, te pegas, se pega, nos pegamos. After de, an action stays in its unchanged dictionary form: un atracón de conducir. The expression is colloquial and often conveys excess or effort.

example.es: Nos pegamos un atracón de documentales.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: jugar con + control, herramienta o idea
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone experiments or plays around with a control, tool, or idea?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of jugar followed by con and name what is being tried in different ways.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Jugar changes for the person and time, while con stays before the thing being adjusted or explored. In this use, jugar does not mean playing a game.

example.en: We are playing around with the design.

applications.explanationEn: En vez de introduces pegarnos as the alternative action that could have been avoided.
Pegarnos identifies us as the people doing too much, while el atracón de conducir names the excessive activity.
Nos is attached to the unchanged dictionary form pegar and the result is written as one word.
Podríamos carries the tentative “we could” meaning, while haber stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Haber is followed by the completed-action form cogido to place the taking before the unrealized possibility.
Nuestras uses the feminine plural form because fotos is feminine plural.

applications.exampleEs: JUGAR CON EL AJUSTE DE "TINTE" DEL PHOTOSHOP
applications.explanationEn: Jugar con presents the Photoshop hue setting as a control to experiment with rather than a game.
Calla is the affirmative informal singular command of callar.
